report.summary: Login failures and OTP not received issues started at 2026-10-13T13:40:00+00:00 because the external dependency otp-provider began returning 503 Service Unavailable errors and experiencing high latency. This caused synchronous authentication requests to fail in auth-service, which cascaded into error rate increases in mobile-bff.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External Third-Party Outage: otp-provider Service Degradation

supporting.note: auth-service error rate spiked sharply from 0.33% to ~33.65% starting precisely at 13:40.
otp-provider error rate spiked from baseline 0.3% to a peak of 80.04% at 13:52, starting precisely at 13:40.
otp-provider p99 latency jumped from 907.65 ms to 5495.16 ms starting at 13:40.
auth-service logs explicitly show OTP send failures because otp-provider responded with 503 Service Unavailable starting at 13:40:13.
mobile-bff error rate increased starting at 13:41 due to its synchronous dependency on auth-service.

contradicting.note: otp-provider request rate remained completely stable with no traffic surges or volume anomalies during the incident window.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Auth-Service v7.1.3 Deployment Bug / Integration Interaction

supporting.note: auth-service v7.1.3 was deployed 35 minutes prior to the onset at 13:05 with changes to limit OTP resends to 3 per 10 minutes.
auth-service logged that OTP resend limits were reached starting at 13:42.

contradicting.note: The primary error is an explicit 503 Service Unavailable returned by otp-provider, and otp-provider metrics independently confirm severe vendor-side degradation starting at the exact same minute (13:40).

facts.text: auth-service error rate spiked to 34.07% starting at 2026-10-13T13:40:00+00:00.
mobile-bff error rate increased to 3.98% starting at 2026-10-13T13:41:00+00:00.
auth-service logs show repeated OTP send failures because otp-provider responded with 503 Service Unavailable, first seen at 2026-10-13T13:40:13+00:00.
auth-service depends synchronously on otp-provider, user-db, and redis-session.
auth-service was deployed at 2026-10-13T13:05:00+00:00 with summary auth-service v7.1.3: limit OTP resends to 3 per 10 minutes.
otp-provider error rate spiked starting at 13:40, going from a baseline of 0.3% to a peak of 80.04% at 13:52.
otp-provider p99 latency spiked starting at 13:40, going from a baseline of 907.65 ms to a peak of 5495.16 ms at 13:56.
otp-provider request rate remained stable with no traffic anomalies during the incident window.

assumptions: The external vendor (otp-provider) experienced internal infrastructure or capacity failures starting at 13:40 independent of client traffic volume.

timeline.event: auth-service v7.1.3 deployed, limiting OTP resends to 3 per 10 minutes
otp-provider error rate and p99 latency spike; auth-service error rate spikes
auth-service logs first OTP send failure due to otp-provider 503 Service Unavailable response
mobile-bff error rate increases due to upstream auth-service dependency failures
auth-service logs that OTP resend limit reached for user

recommended_actions.action: Contact the external otp-provider vendor support to report the 503 Service Unavailable errors and high latency starting at 13:40.
recommended_actions.rationale: External metrics and logs directly show otp-provider is experiencing a major outage.

recommended_actions.action: Implement fallback routing or secondary SMS/OTP vendor integration within auth-service if available.
recommended_actions.rationale: Mitigates total login failure impact when the primary external provider becomes unavailable.

recommended_actions.action: Establish cross-vendor SLA monitoring and automated circuit breakers for external third-party dependencies.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents cascading login failures and improves user feedback transparency during external vendor outages.
